paragraphs.5: This report documents the public P11 launch of Score Companion, its repeatable GitLab delivery pipeline, and production security controls. The live site is separate from the local P10a workflow. P13, not P11, covers the final presentation and timed demo.
paragraphs.7: P11 launch work is listed below. Earlier product-design and integration work is documented in the P10 report.
paragraphs.13: Configured and verified Firebase Hosting, Cloud Run, Google sign-in, persistent storage, GitLab CI/CD, production checks, and launch documentation.
paragraphs.16: Prepared the P11 delivery record; prior core-work contributions remain referenced in the P10 report and team-contributions.md.
paragraphs.24: Firebase Hosting serves the React application over HTTPS. It rewrites API traffic to Cloud Run in us-central1. Cloud Run runs Django, Poppler, Java, and Audiveris; Firestore in Datastore mode stores metadata and private Cloud Storage holds uploaded PDFs and derived images.
paragraphs.25: This managed Google Cloud design keeps the site online independently of a teammate’s laptop while retaining the native PDF-recognition stack. Google sign-in protects each library. GitLab CI builds, tests, deploys, and verifies the same protected-main commit that the public URL serves.

paragraphs.32: Long-running PDF recognition initially blocked short reader requests and produced 429 responses.
paragraphs.33: Kept one Audiveris recognition lock, raised API concurrency to four, reduced polling overlap, and applied user-scoped request limits. The deployment pipeline verified the resulting production service.
paragraphs.34: The original local workflow defaulted to mock profiles rather than the P10a account path.
paragraphs.35: Added local registration, password hashing, sign-in/sign-out, account-scoped ownership, secret-required startup, and production-safe defaults. Backend tests cover registration, login, logout, and account isolation.

paragraphs.50: Score Companion — turn sheet-music PDFs into focused practice measures.
paragraphs.53: 1. Open the URL and continue with a Google account. 2. Upload a PDF or MusicXML score. 3. Wait for conversion, open a measure, and save an optional practice note.
paragraphs.54: 4. Open Practice Review, mark the item practiced, and return to the score. 5. Delete a practice item or score when it is no longer needed.
paragraphs.55: Questions or defects: open an issue in the Team 08 GitLab project.
paragraphs.58: Pipeline configuration: .gitlab-ci.yml; protected main deploys the public build. GitLab is authoritative and GitHub mirrors main.
paragraphs.59: Merge requests run the same checks; pushes to main package images, deploy Cloud Run and Firebase Hosting, then verify the public HTTPS site and session endpoint.
paragraphs.60: Jobs: backend tests and Django deployment check; Firestore integration; frontend lint, tests, and production build; dependency and frontend security scans; container packaging; deploy-production; verify-production.
paragraphs.61: Deployment uses GitLab OpenID Connect and Google Workload Identity Federation, not a committed service-account key. Django’s signing key is a Secret Manager reference. OAuth configuration, hosts, and storage values are supplied by the host/CI; no secret value is committed or bundled in the frontend.
paragraphs.67: Google ID tokens are verified server-side and the stable subject becomes the account owner key. Every score, PDF, image, passage, and practice mark is owner-scoped. Upload type and size are validated; PDF and XML parsing are bounded; CSRF protects writes; cookies are HTTP-only, Secure, and SameSite=Lax in production. CI runs dependency scanning and frontend security checks. The client receives no server-only key.
paragraphs.70: Firebase Hosting provides HTTPS and routes only API traffic to Cloud Run. Cloud Run uses explicit allowed hosts, Firebase-only CORS/CSRF origins, min 0/max 1/concurrency 4, and a private Secret Manager reference. Firestore and the GCS bucket are not public application interfaces. GitLab deploys through a least-privilege federated identity; CI uses immutable images and verifies the public result before cleaning temporary images.
paragraphs.73: This is not a penetration test or compliance certification. Audiveris recognition can require correction. The final required outside-user walkthrough is still pending and is not represented as completed in this report.
